beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: You think the dealer gave you $2,000 off? He didn't. Watch.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Rohan buys a new car, and the dealer slashes $2,000 off the price. But by the last payment, Rohan hands almost all of it back.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: He still needs $33,000, so a bank lends it at 6%. That's $638 a month for 60 months. A fair deal, right?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: But that offer never reaches Rohan. It goes to the dealer first, and the dealer crosses out the rate and writes 8%.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Just $31 extra a month? Who cares? I saved $2,000.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: But count all 60 payments. That small extra grows into $1,868 of interest, almost the whole discount, flowing back out of his wallet.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: And this is the clever part. The bank pays the dealer a cut of that extra interest. So the discount comes off the price, and the loan brings it back, one payment at a time.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: The dealer wins twice: once on the car, and again on the loan. That $1,868 comes out of Rohan's pocket, a little every month.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Still, he gave me $2,000 off. Nice guy, right?
